assumptions: logical construct sequences and modified-site intent are normally known before MR
strands are typically short and deliberately designed to reduce unintended ambiguity
coordinate chain names, residue numbers and ASU cuts are not construct identity
known_edge_cases: short repeated motifs may still occur
three-nucleotide or other constrained repeats may be unavoidable
single-base sticky ends or overhangs may be intrinsically ambiguous
symmetry-related or equivalent ASU cuts may preserve the same construct
unexpected complete or partial ASU copies may occur

authority_order: explicit reviewed registration or registration recipe
authoritative registration of the actual MR solution

allowed_automatic_inference: same-named chains with constant residue-number offsets
unique whole-chain rename with matching chain length and constant residue-number pattern
unique whole-chain rename plus constant residue-number offset
descriptive design-identity evidence for each simple chain candidate is recorded but not used for assignment
refuse_or_defer: multiple equally valid one-to-one chain assignments
chain-count mismatch suggesting split chains, multiplicity or partial copies

descriptive_design_evidence.caution: Target mismatches can be expected PostMR sequence/modification changes and are not a compatibility score.

sequence_and_modification_policy.future_design_aware_inference: Sequence, modified-site intent, sticky-end definitions and other design information may become explicit evidence in later inference layers when they produce a unique reviewed interpretation. They must not become a hidden composite score.
sequence_and_modification_policy.ambiguity_guard: Repeated short motifs and single-base overhangs must remain capable of producing AMBIGUOUS or guided-review outcomes.

timing_policy: cheap non-mutating Registration Scout before MR
ordinary MR first when a candidate remains plausible
authoritative registration on the actual MR solution before PostMR chemistry
bounded explicit Registration/Recut Rescue only when needed

guided_when: more than one non-equivalent mapping remains
a split, recut or boundary operation lacks a reviewed recipe
successful MR candidates imply materially different cuts or multiplicities
mapping depends on topology rather than simple construct correspondence

dimensions: single-copy coordinate realization when directly comparable

guarantees: selection must cover every logical chain
every selected pair must already be a Scout candidate

guided selection does not edit coordinates or promote a global recipe

behavior: enumerate every top-level PDB without selecting one
assess valid and invalid PDBs independently
retain invalid candidates with diagnostics rather than hiding them
record SHA-256 and byte size for every candidate regardless of validity
compute one stable candidate-set fingerprint over selector/status/file identity
run Registration Scout independently on every valid candidate in the read-only scouting layer
multi_pdb_candidate_inventory_v1.current_legacy_behavior: AutoMR still requires one unambiguous nonstandard PDB or an explicit model selector.

human_live_check_queue.policy: Keep the queue small, trigger-based, and tied to real/user-visible behavior rather than duplicating unit tests.

8D93-style non-identity recut live check when executable
8D31-like complete/partial multiplicity live check when executable

shadow_live_validation.interpretation: Registration remained stable while PostMR normalized residue identities to the logical target.
shadow_live_validation.reason_not_completed: Registration was invoked manually/read-only against existing run artifacts rather than through live AutoMR/PostMR integration.

scout.reason: multiple simple one-to-one chain assignments satisfy length/offset rules; Scout v1 refuses sequence-similarity ranking

renamed_real_w_shadow_validation.interpretation: Current conservative ambiguity is scientifically safe; known design intent contains strong discriminating evidence, but that evidence remains non-decisional under Scout v1.

proposed_design_aware_inference_v2.principle: Prefer categorical consistency with declared construct intent over generic sequence-similarity scoring.
candidate_evidence: whether candidate mismatches occur only at sites already declared to change between the family/reference construct and this dataset target
number and identity of unexpected mismatches outside declared-change sites
complete logical-site coverage and one-to-one chain correspondence
proposed_design_aware_inference_v2.suggested_safe_rule: Automatic disambiguation may become eligible only when exactly one complete one-to-one chain mapping has zero unexpected mismatches after accounting for explicitly declared construct-change sites, while every alternative has one or more unexpected mismatches. Otherwise remain AMBIGUOUS.
cautions: do not convert total match count into a weighted score
single-base overhangs and short repeated motifs may remain intrinsically ambiguous
modified-site declarations are intent evidence, not proof of MR correctness
real-data validation is required before promotion into runtime authority

input_evidence: complete simple one-to-one chain assignments from existing length/offset constraints
optional caller-supplied reviewed provider baseline residue codes
design_aware_scout_v2_experiment.proposal_rule: Propose a mapping only when exactly one complete one-to-one chain mapping has zero unexplained mismatches and every alternative has at least one. Never choose merely because it has fewer unexplained mismatches.
fail_closed: logical chain with no simple candidate
design_aware_scout_v2_experiment.provider_baseline_runtime_requirement: Caller-supplied provider codes are experimental evidence only. Runtime use requires binding them to a reviewed/versioned provider or model-family record with provenance.
